headline: Ordered investigations of the officials who prosecuted Trump
why: It only directs the Justice Department how to use powers it already has, so the same kind of order reverses it.

headline: Cancelled 78 Biden executive orders in one stroke
how: Reissue the Biden orders it cancelled.
why: An order that cancels other orders is itself only an order, so a later order can restore or replace what it cancelled.

headline: Shut down federal work to flag online misinformation
why: It directs agencies to stop and review past practice under no statute, so a new order can reverse it.

headline: Told the State Department to put U.S. interests first in diplomacy
how: Rescind the loyalty directive to the Foreign Service.
why: It is a general policy directive to one department that any president issues in some form, with no statute or court behind it.

headline: Shut down every federal diversity, equity and inclusion office
how: Reopen the diversity, equity and inclusion offices.
why: It ended programs the executive branch created by its own policy, not by statute, so a pen can bring them back.

headline: Ordered criminal reviews of ex-officials Trump accused of election meddling
how: End the reviews of former officials.
why: It directs investigative priorities of agencies under presidential authority, so a new order can withdraw the direction.

headline: Opened Alaska lands and waters to drilling, mining and logging
why: It directs agencies to reverse land protections they set themselves; the leases and rules that follow are separate rows.

headline: Froze clean-energy funds and ended the push toward electric cars
how: Restore clean-energy funding and EV goals.
why: It directs agencies on how to use laws already on the books; the budget-law changes to energy credits are separate rows.

headline: Declared a national energy emergency to speed fossil fuel projects
why: A national emergency lasts only as long as the president renews it, so ending it is a presidential act even with lawsuits pending.

headline: Labeled drug cartels and gangs foreign terrorist organizations
why: Designations are made by the Secretary of State and can be revoked the same way; the order only started that process.

headline: Ordered mass deportation enforcement and threatened sanctuary cities
why: It directs agencies to use existing immigration law harder; a pen redirects them while the statutes stay put.

headline: Ordered tougher visa vetting that set up the travel bans
how: End the expanded vetting and travel bans.
why: It orders security reviews and country lists under existing law; the travel bans themselves are separate proclamations, also a pen.

headline: Pulled the United States out of the Paris climate agreement
why: The agreement was joined by executive action without the Senate, so re-entry is a pen too.

headline: Shut down the refugee program and halted approved arrivals
why: Refugee admissions run on presidential determinations under existing law, and the Ninth Circuit largely upheld the pause.

headline: Ordered prosecutors to seek the death penalty wherever possible
how: Restore the federal death penalty pause.
why: It directs charging choices and drug supplies, which are executive discretion, so a pen stops new pursuits.

headline: Shut the border to asylum seekers and restarted Remain in Mexico
how: Restore asylum access at the border.
why: It orders agencies to use border powers Congress already gave them, which a later president can order differently.

headline: Held off enforcing the TikTok law while a sale was arranged
why: It only paused enforcement of a law Congress passed; the sale closed in January 2026, so the pause is spent.

headline: Ordered the military to help seal the border and draft a defense plan
why: It assigns military missions by presidential direction under existing law, so a new order reassigns them.

headline: Ended federal recognition of transgender people
how: Restore transgender recognition on federal documents.
why: No statute fixes the federal definition of sex; this order does, so a pen resets it, apart from any rules agencies wrote under it.

headline: Froze all U.S. foreign aid pending a review
why: The directive is a pen; the lapsed money and the shuttered aid agency are separate, harder rows.

headline: Rewrote federal hiring, adding essay questions on the president's agenda
why: Hiring practice is set by presidential order and personnel-office guidance, not statute, so a new order and new guidance replace it.

headline: Made tens of thousands of career civil servants fireable at will
why: The order told the personnel office to write a rule, now final, so repeal also needs new rulemaking.

headline: Renamed the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America and Denali Mount McKinley
how: Put the Gulf of Mexico and Denali back on the map.
why: A name change is housekeeping that costs nothing to keep and nothing is lost by it.

headline: Pulled the United States out of the World Health Organization
why: Congress set the terms of membership in 1948, and a joint resolution with no budget effect needs sixty Senate votes.

headline: Renamed the Digital Service as DOGE and gave it access to federal systems
why: It only reshapes offices the president controls, while the staff and spending cuts it led to are separate, harder rows.

headline: Stripped citizenship from babies born here to undocumented parents
how: Nothing to undo: the Supreme Court struck it down.
why: It stays in the pen bucket because it is an order, but the Court, not any president, ended it.

headline: Ended federal contractor affirmative action and targeted diversity programs
why: Contractor affirmative-action rules rest on an executive order, not a statute, and civil rights laws stay in place either way.

headline: Revoked the federal COVID vaccine mandate and contractor safety rules
why: It cancelled two 2021 COVID orders that Biden's own administration had already wound down, so there is little to restore.

headline: Labeled the Houthis a foreign terrorist organization
why: A Democratic president would likely keep a designation of a group that attacks shipping; it is made and lifted by the State Department.

headline: Ordered release of the JFK, RFK and Martin Luther King assassination files
why: Releasing public records harms no one, and a pen cannot recall what is already out.

headline: Re-established the president's science and technology advisory council
why: An advisory council is housekeeping that every president sets up in some form, and a new president can reshape it by order.

headline: Rolled back crypto oversight and banned a federal digital dollar
why: It sets agency direction and a working group by presidential order; the stablecoin law that followed is a separate statute.

headline: Revoked Biden's AI safety order and ordered a plan to speed up AI
why: It withdrew a Biden order and told agencies to write an AI plan, all by presidential direction, so the same instrument reverses it.

headline: Set up a council to recommend shrinking or abolishing FEMA
why: A review council is created and dissolved by presidential order, though FEMA itself exists in statute and stays unless Congress acts.

headline: Ordered California dam water sent to farms, overriding fish protections
how: Restore the river and fish protections.
why: It directs federal water operations and agency reviews by presidential order, while laws like the Endangered Species Act still apply.

headline: Revoked Biden's orders protecting abortion access and travel for care
why: It revoked two Biden orders and tells the budget office how to apply the Hyde rider; both are presidential acts, and the rider is law.

headline: Banned transgender people from military service
how: Lift the ban on transgender service.
why: Who may serve is set by Defense policy under presidential direction, not statute; the ban is in effect while lawsuits continue.

headline: Reinstated troops discharged for refusing the COVID vaccine, with back pay
why: Congress had already repealed the military vaccine mandate, and reinstating the discharged troops harms no one.

headline: Ended diversity programs across the military and service academies
why: Those programs were set by Defense policy under presidential direction, not by statute, so a pen can bring them back.

headline: Ordered a missile defense shield over the whole country, Golden Dome
why: Missile defense has bipartisan roots, and the order mostly directs a plan; the spending is Congress's call, not this order's.

headline: Cut federal funds for hospitals giving transgender youth care
why: It directs agencies on grants and enforcement without changing a statute, so a pen cancels the order itself; a court has blocked it.

headline: Targeted foreign students and universities over campus Gaza protests
how: Stop the campus deportation and funding threats.
why: It directs agencies to use existing civil-rights and immigration law; a pen redirects them, and one court rejected a challenge to the order.

headline: Created a task force for the 250th birthday and a statue garden
why: A commemoration task force is ceremonial, and a later president would run the anniversary on his own terms anyway.

headline: Threatened school funding over lessons on race and gender identity
why: It conditions federal school money by presidential direction, not statute, so a pen reverses it; a court partly blocked it in October 2025.

headline: Pushed federal money toward private and religious school choice
how: Redirect school funds to public schools.
why: It orders agencies to issue guidance on existing education funds; Congress controls the money, so a pen reverses the guidance.

headline: Required agencies to repeal ten rules for every new one
why: It is an internal management directive to agencies, which a later president can swap for a different one.

headline: Put a 25 percent tax on most imports from Canada
how: Nothing to undo: the Supreme Court ended it.
why: It stays pen because it is an order, but the Court held emergency powers allow no tariffs; refunds are being sorted out in court.

headline: Put a 25 percent tax on most imports from Mexico
how: Nothing to undo: the Supreme Court ended it.
why: It stays pen because it is an order, but the Court held emergency powers allow no tariffs; refunds are being sorted out in court.

headline: Put a 10 percent tax on imports from China
how: Nothing to undo: the Supreme Court ended it.
why: It stays pen because it is an order, but the Court held emergency powers allow no tariffs; refunds are being sorted out in court.

headline: Ordered a plan for a U.S. sovereign wealth fund
why: It orders only a plan, with nothing yet created or spent, and Congress would have to approve any fund.

headline: Delayed the Canada tariffs after border pledges
why: It only postponed a tariff step, the pause is over, and the tariffs themselves are covered by their own rows.

headline: Delayed the Mexico tariffs after border pledges
why: It only postponed a tariff step, the pause is over, and the tariffs themselves are covered by their own rows.

headline: Quit the UN Human Rights Council and ordered cuts to UN agencies
why: It launched a review of memberships; the withdrawals that followed are their own rows, and treaty-based ones may need the Senate.

headline: Delayed the end of duty-free small packages from China
why: It only postponed a step; a later order ended duty-free treatment, and that later order carries the real change as its own row.

headline: Barred transgender girls and women from girls' and women's school sports
how: Restore transgender athletes' access to sports.
why: It sets enforcement priorities under an existing law; the Supreme Court upheld state sports bans in 2026 but did not rule on this order.

headline: Created a federal task force on anti-Christian bias
why: A task force is created and disbanded by order, and its work is reports and recommendations rather than binding rules.

headline: Sanctioned International Criminal Court officials
why: Sanctions under the emergency powers act are imposed by order and lifted by order; courts have blocked it only for some plaintiffs.

headline: Cut off aid to South Africa and fast-tracked refugee status for Afrikaners
how: Restore South Africa aid and end the Afrikaner priority.
why: Aid and refugee priorities are set by presidential direction under existing law, and no court has ruled on this order.

headline: Created a White House Faith Office
how: Restore the Office of Faith-Based Partnerships.
why: A White House staff office is housekeeping that every president organizes as he likes, with no statute or court involved.

headline: Ordered a review of federal gun rules to loosen firearm limits
why: It directs the Justice Department to review Biden-era actions; gun statutes are untouched, so a new order restores the earlier approach.

headline: Closed the Federal Executive Institute, a school for senior civil servants
why: It closed a small training center by order; reopening it would cost money for little gain, and no statute is involved.

headline: Ordered federal offices to stop buying paper straws
why: It is a purchasing preference with no real stakes for anyone, and a pen can swap it whenever it matters.

headline: Paused enforcement of the anti-bribery law for overseas deals
why: It directs prosecutors' priorities; the bribery law itself is untouched, so a pen restores enforcement.

headline: Ordered agencies to plan mass layoffs and shrink the federal workforce
why: It tells agencies to plan layoffs, which the Supreme Court allowed to proceed, so the order is a pen but completed cuts stay.

headline: Made diplomats subject to firing for not carrying out presidential policy
why: It orders State to reform personnel rules by presidential direction; the Foreign Service Act still governs, so a new order resets practice.

headline: Created a commission on childhood chronic disease run by the health secretary
why: A study commission makes reports, not binding rules; any rules that follow are separate rows.

headline: Created a council to speed up oil, gas and coal production
why: A White House council is created and dissolved by presidential order, with no statute behind it.

headline: Barred federal funds for schools that require COVID-19 vaccines
how: Let schools set their own vaccine rules again.
why: Almost no school requires the shot, so the order changes little in practice and reversing it gains little.

headline: Ordered proposals to make IVF fertility treatment easier to get
why: It asks for policy recommendations to expand access, which a Democratic president would welcome rather than reverse.

headline: Put independent agencies like the FTC and SEC under White House control
how: Stop White House review of agency rules.
why: The Court's 2026 holding in Trump v. Slaughter lets presidents fire independent-agency heads; only a constitutional change reverses that.

headline: Gutted four small agencies including the U.S. Institute of Peace
why: It orders agencies Congress created to shrink to the legal minimum, so a new president can restore their staff and grants.

headline: Cut federal benefits and grants that reach undocumented immigrants
why: It directs agencies on how to read existing benefit laws, so a new reading by order replaces it, though part is already blocked.
